description: DELETE-USER-INFO's own first EVALUATE arm at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:177-182 - re-entry with PF5 pressed and USRIDINI transmitted as SPACES, which is the SPACES half of the compound '= SPACES OR LOW-VALUES' condition at :177. THIS IS THE ONLY PATH ON WHICH A DELETE IS REQUESTED AND YET GENUINELY NEVER RUNS: every other arm of the EVALUATE EIBAID at :108-130 never performs DELETE-USER-INFO at all, and the only other route through DELETE-USER-INFO - the WHEN OTHER at :183-185, which moves the cursor and CONTINUEs with the flag still off - always reaches :190 and :191. The path is reached through the ELSE at :106 because CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1 and CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is therefore already true at :95, so :96-105 is skipped and RECEIVE-USRDEL-SCREEN runs at :107. RECEIVE-USRDEL-SCREEN at :232-238 captures RESP and RESP2 and then NEVER EVALUATES THEM; that is reproduced as written and no receive-failure branch is invented. The EVALUATE EIBAID at :108-130 is ordered and its FOURTH arm matches - DFHENTER at :109, DFHPF3 at :111 and DFHPF4 at :119 are all tested first, DFHPF12 at :123 and WHEN OTHER at :126 are never reached - so DELETE-USER-INFO is performed at :122. Inside it :178 raises WS-ERR-FLG to 'Y', :179-180 moves 'User ID can NOT be empty...' into WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80), :181 moves -1 into USRIDINL and :182 performs SEND-USRDEL-SCREEN exactly once. THE DECISIVE GUARD IS :188: 'IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON' is now FALSE, so the entire block :189-191 is skipped - the MOVE USRIDINI TO SEC-USR-ID at :189 never happens, READ-USER-SEC-FILE at :190 never runs, and DELETE-USER-SEC-FILE at :191 never runs either. THERE IS NO DATASET ACCESS WHATSOEVER ON THIS PATH - no readForUpdate, no deleteHeld, nothing - which is why expectedWrites is empty and all ten seeded rows are pinned unchanged at zero-based indices 0-9: 'nothing happened to USRSEC' is asserted positively rather than left implicit. Gate G47 consequently has NO CALL SITE here, so no FileStatus outcome and no forcedOutcome is declared; fabricating one would assert an I/O path this arm does not take. THIS CASE IS THE COMPLEMENT OF case13.json AND ONLY THE TWO TOGETHER PIN THE :188-192 CONTROL STRUCTURE UNAMBIGUOUSLY: case13 presses the same PF5 key but with a non-blank identifier, so the guard IS entered, BOTH PERFORMs execute, and DELETE-USER-SEC-FILE at :191 fires even though READ-USER-SEC-FILE at :190 has already failed - because no second guard sits between the two - which is why it reaches the dataset with its locking read, emits a DISPLAY line at :330 as well as its message, and repaints over two sends. Here the blank-identifier validation raises the flag BEFORE :188, so the guard is never entered, NEITHER PERFORM executes, the dataset is never reached by any operation at all, and a single logical message is emitted over a single send with no DISPLAY line. Removing either case would leave a translation free to add the missing guard, or to hoist the read above the validation, without any case failing. The single send carries all eleven xxxO items: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :243-262 paints TRNNAMEO, TITLE01O, PGMNAMEO, TITLE02O, CURDATEO and CURTIMEO, then :217 moves WS-MESSAGE into ERRMSGO PIC X(78), an 80-to-78 right truncation, which is why the ONE logical message is pinned on its TWO declared channels at their own widths rather than compared across widths - WS_MESSAGE_80 holds it padded to eighty and SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 holds its first seventy-eight characters, and a move that truncated on the left would fail the second while still passing the first. There is exactly ONE logical message here and NO DISPLAY line at all: neither WHEN OTHER arm - :293-299 of the read or :329-335 of the delete - is reached, because neither paragraph runs. The message literal is byte-identical to case05.json's and case06.json's, deliberately, because DELETE-USER-INFO's EVALUATE TRUE at :176-186 is a textual duplicate of PROCESS-ENTER-KEY's at :144-154 - same condition, same text, same MOVE -1 TO USRIDINL - and encoding it identically documents that duplication faithfully while the differing I/O consequences are what case13 and this case pin down. USRIDINO is transmitted blank because the request carried it blank. FNAMEO, LNAMEO and USRTYPEO carry back the STALE values the RECEIVE delivered, UNALTERED AND ON PURPOSE: DELETE-USER-INFO has no equivalent of PROCESS-ENTER-KEY's MOVE SPACES TO FNAMEI LNAMEI USRTYPEI at :157-159, and INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :349-356 runs only on the delete's NORMAL arm at :315 and on PF4 at :343. Deliberately non-blank request values are declared so that the absence of any clearing is observable - had they been declared blank, a translation that wrongly cleared them would still have passed. ERRMSGC is NOT written on this arm - DFHNEUTR is moved only at :285 when the lookup succeeds and DFHGREEN only at :317 when the delete succeeds, and neither line executes here - so the colour asserted is DFHDFCOL, the default that survives where nothing was moved, and the field keeps the BMS-declared ERRMSG ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET) COLOR=RED of app/bms/COUSR03.bms:140-143. The offending field is marked the only way this program marks one: COUSR03C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY - its eight COPY statements at :49-68 are COCOM01Y, COUSR03, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CSUSR01Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - so it sets attributes and tests EIBAID inline, and the MOVE -1 TO USRIDINL at :181 is the cursor and therefore the highlight, pinned as cursorField. This is REENTER state carrying an error, so the DFHRED-and-asterisk highlight applies, and it rides on USRIDINA and USRIDINF, which are attribute metadata and never payload members. Attribute and AID mnemonics come from common.BmsAttributes and common.CicsAid because DFHBMSCA and DFHAID are IBM-supplied and absent from this repository, which is risk R-D. The transaction ends at :134-137 with EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CU03') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), so the termination is RETURN_TRANSID rather than XCTL and no nextProgram other than this program's own name is named; every field of the commarea travels back in the payload - no server-side session state exists, which is rule R6 and gate G37 asserted directly rather than assumed. PROVENANCE: every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the sources named below and is NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL. Running it is empirically impossible in this environment - no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed-file handler as disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository - which is the documented eight-blocker deviation escalated as risk R-A; it changes the provenance of the expected values and nothing else. Derived from app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:174-192 - specifically the blank-identifier arm at :177-182 and the guard at :188 - together with :213-225, cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:18-23 (8+20+20+8+1 = 57 plus SEC-USR-FILLER's 23 = 80), app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44 with app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:50-58 (160 + 34 = 194 bytes), app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY where COUSR3AO REDEFINES COUSR3AI so the eleven xxxO items overlay the eleven xxxI items and no password item exists on either side, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy for both forty-character titles, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS header shapes, app/bms/COUSR03.bms for the declared field attributes, and the ten in-stream rows of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose 57-character width against the LRECL=80 RECFM=FB of :48 and the RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) of :65-66 is exactly what the declared normalisation supplies. The literal PASSWORD in SEC-USR-PWD is legacy sample data carried byte for byte because CSUSR01Y places it inside the eighty bytes; plaintext credentials are an inherited property of the legacy design rather than a choice made here, this screen has no password field and this path never reads or paints the span, and no hashing, encoding or token is introduced. The full ten-row seed is declared even though this case never reads it, so that the unchanged-dataset assertion PROVES the absence of I/O rather than assuming it. The dataset is addressed only by its binding key, never by a dataset name. The seed, the pinned 2022-07-19T23:12:35 clock, the six record field names and the 57-to-80 normalisation are reused byte for byte from case01.json.
